newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state polls use motor home after bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state polls use motor home after bomb threat.

text.p: Voters made their election choices in a motor home Tuesday after a polling place for two precincts had to be evacuated because of bomb threats, officials said.

Cathy Pearsall-Stipek, Pierce County auditor, said election officials and voters had to be evacuated along with students after two bomb threats were called in to Spanaway Lake High School about 2 p.m. PST (5 p.m. EST).
Election officials grabbed their books, ballot boxes and booths and relocated to a car about a half-mile away.
"A nice gentleman came out and had a motor home and allowed us to set up a polling place in his motor home," Pearsall-Stipek said. Officials marked the vehicle with a large sign saying "Vote Here."
Officials did not know whether they would be allowed to return to the school.
"All we know is, people are continuing to vote," the auditor said.
